entities.summary: Comets have been a source of fascination and mystique for centuries, with recorded observations dating back to ancient civilizations. One of the earliest recorded cometary observations was made by the ancient Chinese astronomer Shi Shen in 2400 BCE, who described a comet that was visible in the sky. This event was noted in the Shu Jing, a collection of ancient Chinese texts that contain some of the earliest recorded records of cometary activity. Comets were also a major focus of interest during the Renaissance, with scientists such as Johannes Kepler and Isaac Newton studying the orbits and behavior of comets. In modern times, comets have been the subject of extensive scientific study, with spacecraft such as NASA's Deep Impact and the European Space Agency's Rosetta missions providing new insights into the composition and origins of comets. The discovery of water vapor on Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko by the Rosetta mission has significant implications for the search for life beyond Earth, and the study of comets continues to be an active area of research in astronomy and planetary science.
